properties.statement:
THREE PLACES WHERE THE SERVER KNOWS THE ANSWER AND MAKES THE CALLER GUESS. Reported across both 2026-09-04 documents, and one of them was reproduced here the same day without looking for it.

① `withdraw_question` RETURNS `{withdrawn: false}` WITH NO REASON. dev_storyflow: 'A false with no `why` costs a round-trip of guessing; the gap tools already carry reasons in their replies, so this is the odd one out.' CONFIRMED at `tools/ask.rs:348` — the reply is literally `json!({ "withdrawn": found, "gap_id": req.gap_id })`. A bare boolean. They closed the question through `acknowledge_gap` instead.

② `export_graph` REFUSES THE PATH IT ITSELF WROTE LAST TIME. dev_storyflow: 'Every session ends by exporting to `.reflow2/design.export.json`; every export now needs `overwrite=true` on a second call, since the first refuses. THE REPLY ALREADY RETURNS `prev_content_hash`, SO THE SERVER KNOWS THE FILE ON DISK IS ITS OWN PREVIOUS EXPORT. A refusal is right when the file is somebody else's; when the hash matches the server's own last export, overwrite is the only sensible action and should be the default.'

⭐⭐ REPRODUCED HERE, UNPROMPTED, SIX TIMES IN ONE DAY. Every `export_graph` call in this session — three ordinary exports and the v0.47.1 release cut — passed `overwrite: true` as a reflex, against a file this same seat had written minutes earlier and whose hash the reply then echoed back as `prev_content_hash`. The guard exists for BL-57, to stop a stray or injected path destroying a file; it does not distinguish that case from the seat overwriting its own last export, which is the only thing it ever actually does.

③ EVERY `acknowledge_gap` WARNS THAT IT CARRIES NOBODY'S NAME. qs 2026-09-04: 'A Contributor for the user existed (THE LENS NAMED IT) and I did not pass it; the tool could default `approver` to the session's contributor rather than warn each time.' The server knows who the session belongs to — it served the lens that named them.

⭐ ONE MECHANISM: A GUARD THAT CANNOT TELL THE DANGEROUS CASE FROM THE ONLY CASE. Each of the three is a correct caution aimed at a real hazard — an unexplained withdrawal, a clobbered file, an unattributed judgement — and each fires identically on the overwhelmingly common safe case, which the server has the information to recognise and does not check. The result is a reflex: callers pass `overwrite: true` without reading, and ignore a warning that appears every time. A caution that fires on correct work is a caution that gets switched off, which is the same argument `sync_debt` makes about its own gate and `unexported_work` was rebuilt around this morning.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether defaulting the acknowledgement approver is SAFE. `dec:certainty-derived` forbids the agent forging the user's signature on a status, and an acknowledgement is a judgement — so 'the session's contributor' may be exactly the attribution that must stay explicit. That is a ruling, not an implementation, and it is the user's.
